question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2\operatorname{arsech}⁡({x}^{2})] \\  & =2\cdot [-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1-{({x}^{2})}^{2}}}]\cdot {({x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1-{x}^{4}}}\cdot 2x \\  & =-\frac{4}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
